answer: A jetty only lets boats dock after they tie up and pay a berth fee; an agent economy can work the same way. Every new identity must lock a refundable stake, a small ember of value that stays bonded while it earns. If peers catch it running duplicate identities or spamming, the stake is slashed and the identity is burned. Like yarrow spreading only where the soil is tended, honest agents grow reputation on one bonded identity, while an attacker must pay a fresh stake for every fake, so a thousand Sybils cost a thousand stakes and the attack stops paying for itself.
